alysha brilla.bio:
Ontario singer-songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist Alysha Brilla has built an independent career around a blend of soul, folk, pop and globally rooted rhythmic traditions. Raised in the Great Lakes region with Indo-Tanzanian and Irish-Scottish Canadian family roots, Brilla developed a musical language shaped by both diasporic culture and contemporary studio craft. Her early solo albums established her as a self-directed writer and producer rather than only a front-of-mic performer, with In My Head earning a JUNO nomination for Adult Contemporary Album of the Year.

Brilla followed with Womyn and Rooted, both extending her focus on identity, gender, ancestry and community while deepening the production side of her work. Womyn received another JUNO nomination, and Rooted brought a third. Her production work also earned recognition at the Independent Music Awards, while collaborations and studio credits have connected her with artists including Bedouin Soundclash and Digging Roots. That combination of songwriting and technical authorship is central to her significance: Brilla has consistently foregrounded the role of women and gender-diverse creators behind the console as well as onstage.

Her work later expanded into film composition and education. Brilla composed the original score for Fawzia Mirza's The Queen of My Dreams, earning a 2024 Canadian Screen Award nomination, and has taught and spoken about music production, representation and creative practice at institutions including Berklee College of Music. By 2025 she had also been recognized by Women in Music for international leadership. Brilla's place in Canadian music is therefore broader than any one record: she represents an independent model in which performance, production, cultural identity, mentorship and advocacy remain part of the same artistic practice.
alysha brilla.directory_summary: Ontario artist, producer and multi-instrumentalist Alysha Brilla has built a distinctly independent career blending soul, folk, pop and globally rooted rhythms. Albums including In My Head, Womyn and Rooted brought three JUNO nominations, while her production work and advocacy have helped expand the visibility of women and gender-diverse creators behind the console. She later composed the score for The Queen of My Dreams, earning a 2024 Canadian Screen Award nomination and extending her work into film and education.

alyssa reid.bio:
Edmonton-born and Ontario-raised singer-songwriter Alyssa Reid moved from teenage talent-show exposure into one of the more distinctive Canadian pop breakthroughs of the early 2010s. After appearing on The Next Star, she signed with Wax Records and released "Alone Again," a reworking of Heart's 1987 hit "Alone" featuring Canadian rapper P. Reign. The single became a major Canadian radio record, reached the Top 20 of the Canadian Hot 100 and later crossed into the United Kingdom, where it reached No. 2. Its success drove Reid's 2011 debut album The Game and earned her a 2012 JUNO nomination for New Artist of the Year.

Rather than disappearing after the scale of that first hit, Reid continued developing as both an artist and songwriter. Time Bomb arrived in 2014 with a more personal singer-songwriter emphasis, while later releases moved between polished pop, piano balladry and darker electronic production. She also spent a period releasing music under the name ASHS, using the alias to explore a moodier pop vocabulary away from the expectations attached to "Alone Again." Across those shifts, Reid maintained a strong connection to songwriting as the through-line of her career.

That writing work has increasingly become part of her wider significance. Reid has written for other Canadian and international pop artists, including Virginia to Vegas, bülow and Alessia Cara, extending her impact beyond her own recordings. A decade after "Alone Again," Billboard Canada noted that the song had sold more than a million copies worldwide and accumulated tens of millions of streams. Reid's career captures a particular early-2010s Canadian pop moment when domestic radio, MuchMusic visibility and international licensing could turn a homegrown single into a cross-border hit while also opening a longer career behind the scenes.
alyssa reid.directory_summary: Edmonton-born, Ontario-raised singer-songwriter Alyssa Reid broke internationally with 2011's "Alone Again," a Canadian radio smash that later reached No. 2 in the U.K. and helped earn her a JUNO nomination for New Artist of the Year. After debut album The Game, Reid continued through Time Bomb, later experimented under the ASHS name and developed a substantial songwriting career for artists including Virginia to Vegas, bülow and Alessia Cara.

anjulie.bio:
Oakville, Ontario singer-songwriter Anjulie Persaud emerged in the late 2000s with a pop sound shaped by R&B, electronic production and the reggae and calypso she heard growing up in an Indo-Guyanese household. Her 2009 debut album introduced "Boom," a sleek, percussion-driven single that brought her early television and radio exposure and established her as a Canadian pop artist with a strong songwriting identity. She followed with singles including "Brand New Chick" and "You and I," moving further toward dance-pop while retaining the rhythmic instincts that distinguished her from much of the country's singer-songwriter mainstream.

"Brand New Chick" became one of her largest Canadian hits, reaching the Top 20 of the Canadian Hot 100, earning platinum certification and receiving a 2012 JUNO nomination for Dance Recording of the Year. Anjulie's career also expanded well beyond her own catalogue. She built a parallel reputation as a songwriter, contributing to material recorded by artists including Kelly Clarkson, Nicki Minaj, Cassie and Icona Pop and collaborating across pop and electronic music with producers and artists such as Zedd, Diplo and Benny Benassi.

That dual role is what gives Anjulie an important place in modern Canadian pop. Her own recordings connected the late-2000s singer-songwriter world to the EDM-heavy pop that followed, while her behind-the-scenes writing placed a Canadian voice inside a much larger international hit-making network. She has continued releasing independently and collaborating across electronic and alternative pop, making her career less about one sustained commercial era than about adaptability across songwriting, performance and production-driven pop culture.
anjulie.directory_summary: Oakville singer-songwriter Anjulie moved from the R&B- and reggae-informed pop of "Boom" into dance-pop with the platinum Canadian hit "Brand New Chick," which earned a 2012 JUNO nomination. Her impact extends well beyond her own releases: she has written and collaborated across mainstream pop and electronic music with artists including Kelly Clarkson, Nicki Minaj, Icona Pop, Zedd and Diplo, making her an important Canadian bridge between artist-led pop and the international songwriting network.
